note: Semantic classes for physical merchandise intelligence. Typical dimensions are real-world defaults in inches used only when the catalogue carries no dimensions; catalogue dimensions always win. spatial_role_candidates map to the 3M.3 SpatialRole enum (plus GROUND for rugs).

S.note: vases, bowls, table lamps, mantel clocks, china pieces

M.note: side tables, dining/side chairs, small sculpture, framed prints

L.note: wingback/arm chairs, consoles, desks, chests, large paintings, tall clocks

XL.note: sofas, cabinets, breakfronts, floor lamps, beds, dining tables

attribute_definitions.anchor_weight: 0 accent · 1 supporting · 2 secondary anchor · 3 primary anchor
attribute_definitions.foreground_suitability: 0 never in front · 1 rarely · 2 suitable · 3 ideal foreground accent
attribute_definitions.can_support / can_be_supported_by: class names; parenthesised annotations are human notes and are stripped by the loader
attribute_definitions.allowable_overlap: as_front: what this object may overlap when it is nearer; as_back: what may overlap it when it is farther
attribute_definitions.prohibited_relations: THROUGH (silhouettes cross interiors on the same plane), FLOATING (no support/baseline), ON:x (resting where it cannot), SCALE conditions, family exclusions
attribute_definitions.dominant_ground_object: sets the scene scale and is never overlapped except by foreground accents at its lower edge

classes.notes: Major floor anchor. Nothing sits on it except cushions/throws. A side table beside the arm may touch the arm silhouette at the edge but never cross the seat.
Medium/large floor anchor. Side table is a companion BESIDE it; the table silhouette may touch the outer arm edge but must not cross seat, arm or wing.
Pushed-in chairs may overlap a dining table's lower edge/apron; never its top.
Smaller companion to seating; BESIDE a chair or sofa arm; top height ≈ arm height; never larger than the seating it accompanies.
Central horizontal anchor in front of seating; overlaps the sofa's lower edge only.
Against a wall; art or mirror hangs above it.
Major horizontal floor anchor; chairs belong with it.
Large rear vertical anchor (breakfront, armoire, china cabinet). Always grounded; always behind.
Supported by a table/console; base sits on the support's top band.
Floor-supported vertical, beside or behind seating; taller than any chair.
Ceiling plane; shown high, never resting on anything.
Tabletop/shelf/pedestal/foreground. A floor vase (≥ 24 in) is a distinct class instance: plane floor, anchor 1.
China is treated as a grouped tabletop/shelf set (a stack, a place setting), never scattered on the floor plane.
Scale-dependent: under 20 in → table/pedestal.
Over 36 in → floor or pedestal; behaves as a floor anchor.
Wall plane. Hangs above furniture; may lean against a wall/cabinet only when declared 'leaning' (then baseline on the floor and tilt shown).
As painting; a leaning floor mirror is declared 'leaning'.
Ground plane under furniture. Rendered as a floor patch beneath anchors, never over them; never vertical unless the lot is a hung textile.
Heavy ground anchor.
Dominant ground object; sets the scene scale; nothing overlaps it except foreground accents at its lower edge.
Close-up / category composition only (CATEGORY_GROUP lineup, tile or hero). Never placed at room scale beside furniture.
Wall plane in scene families; free placement only in CATALOG_SCATTER.

class_resolution.source: lot.category_key + title/description keyword rules + (optional) image classifier; confidence stored; unresolved → generic class by size (from image aspect + category family) with anchor_weight 1 and foreground_suitability 1
class_resolution.owner_review: a creative whose scene contains any unresolved class in an anchor position is Owner-review flagged
